key_insight: The minimum perturbation energy needed to trigger pipe-flow turbulence decreases as O(Re^-3), even though the transition pathway stays qualitatively similar and becomes more localized at higher Reynolds number.
engineering_relevance: For pipe systems, this provides a predictive scaling law for robustness to disturbances, helping estimate transition risk and design flow-control strategies across Reynolds numbers.
method: Variationally computed nonlinear optimal perturbations to laminar pipe flow.
Analyzed the transition pathway through Orr growth, nonlinear oblique-wave interaction, and lift-up.
Measured how perturbation thickness, energy gain, and transition threshold scale with Reynolds number up to Re<=5000.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computed results up to Re<=5000 showing δ_r ∝ Re^-1/3, Orr-phase gain ∝ Re, nonlinear-stage gain ∝ Re^2, and a Reynolds-independent transition threshold that implies minimal energy scales as O(Re^-3).
watch_item: The scaling is demonstrated within a finite Reynolds-number range and for optimal perturbations in an idealized pipe-flow setting, so applicability to real disturbances may require validation.
paper_title: Scaling of the minimal energy for turbulence transition in pipe flow
